long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Omaha, Scott studied civil engineering at Colorado State and joined Peter Kiewit Sons' after military service. He began as an intern and spent decades in operating roles, improving districts and expanding the contractor in Canada before succeeding Peter Kiewit as chairman and chief executive in 1979. Kiewit's employee-ownership structure allowed Scott to become a major shareholder through his career rather than through family inheritance.

Under Scott, Kiewit moved beyond construction into power and fiber-optic communications. The company developed MFS, took it public and distributed its remaining shares to Kiewit stockholders; Scott then chaired telecom successor Level 3. He also helped take MidAmerican Energy private with Berkshire Hathaway and remained a significant family shareholder and director of the business later called Berkshire Hathaway Energy. By his death in 2021, energy was the largest identified component of his wealth, while telecom had been central to its earlier creation. Scott also transferred substantial resources to philanthropy. Foundation endowments, utility assets, Kiewit's projects and listed-company values belonged to their entities, not directly to him.
